headline: The War Horse reports that newly obtained Department of War records provide the most detailed public accounting to date of U.S. casualties during the opening phase of the Iran war, revealing 400+ casualty incidents between Feb. 28 and April 8, including at least 17 life-threatening injuries. The data shows head trauma was the single most common injury, with at least 170 cases, raising concerns that traumatic brain injury (TBI) could become the conflict's defining wound. The War Horse also reports several previously undisclosed mass casualty events, including 70 casualties on March 18 and 29 casualties on March 3, that were never publicly detailed by U.S. Central Command. Two generals-Brig. Gen. Clint Barnes and Maj. Gen. Brad Hinson-were among those who sustained head injuries during the March 1 drone strike on Port Shuaiba, Kuwait. The reporting also aligns with @TheIntelFrog's documentation of medical evacuation flights throughout Operation Epic Fury in near real time, repeatedly noting that the tempo of those flights suggested the number of U.S. casualties was rising beyond the figures publicly acknowledged by the Department of War. These newly released records provide independent evidence consistent with that assessment. Source: https://thewarhorse.org/records-troops-wounded-iran-war/

headline: Reuters reports that Iran is expected to receive its first shipment of 300–400 Chinese-made shoulder-fired air defense systems (MANPADS) within weeks, marking one of Tehran's largest known efforts to rebuild its short-range air defenses since the war with the U.S. and Israel began. According to Reuters, the reported $60–70 million deal includes QW-12 and FN-16 infrared-guided missiles designed to defend against low-flying aircraft, helicopters, and drones. Their mobility makes them more difficult to target than fixed air defense sites that have been repeatedly struck during the conflict. China's Foreign Ministry denied the report, calling it "completely groundless," while Pakistan rejected claims it would facilitate deliveries through its territory. The report also comes just days after President Trump said he does not believe China is providing military assistance to Iran. If confirmed, however, the procurement would represent a significant expansion of Iran's short-range air defense capabilities and could indicate growing defense cooperation between Tehran and Beijing despite Beijing's public denials. Source: https://www.reuters.com/world/china/iran-get-chinese-shoulder-launched-missile-systems-weeks-sources-say-2026-07-29/

headline: Axios reports that senior Trump administration officials believe sustained economic pressure may ultimately inflict more damage on Iran than an expanded bombing campaign, pointing to growing signs of financial strain inside the country. According to Axios, U.S. officials cite intelligence indicating Iran is struggling to fund proxy forces, facing gasoline shortages, and under increasing financial pressure from sanctions led by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. Officials argue those economic measures, combined with a U.S. naval blockade, could prove more effective over time than additional airstrikes. Axios also reports Iran continues to seek sanctions relief and access to frozen assets through indirect talks mediated by Oman, Qatar, and Pakistan, while the Trump administration insists any agreement must also address Tehran's remaining nuclear material. The report notes President Trump's decision to pause strikes followed military concerns over air defense interceptor stockpiles but says officials characterize those warnings as a risk assessment rather than the primary driver of the decision.
